description: MCP `tools/list` manifest for the 13 tools exposed by `mnm mcp serve`, in canonical registration order (search pair, chunk reads, document reads, corpus discovery, diagnostics, local install). Each tool's name, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, and annotations are part of the public contract per Constitution I and FR-037. The runtime manifest at `crates/mnm-mcp/src/tools.rs::list()` is the single source of truth: the `tools` key below is generated from it verbatim (MCP wire format) and enforced by `crates/mnm-mcp/tests/contract_sync.rs`. Regenerate with `REGENERATE_CONTRACT=1 cargo test -p mnm-mcp --test contract_sync`. Embedded schemas use JSON Schema draft 2020-12. A success result carries one text content block (summary plus a fenced trimmed-JSON view) and full-fidelity `structuredContent` conforming to the tool's outputSchema, including `suggested_next_actions`; failures use the shared envelope described under `error_envelope`.

auth_reason.description: AUTH_FAILED only: invalid_credentials (401 — invalid/expired Midnight token; recover via `mnm auth github`), insufficient_tier (403 — valid token, request not permitted for the account, typically an access-tier restriction), or invalid_embedding_key (BYOK embed/rerank — VoyageAI rejected your VOYAGE_API_KEY; set a valid VOYAGE_API_KEY, not `mnm auth github`).

client_model.description: EMBEDDING_MODEL_MISMATCH only: the {name}@{revision} the client embedded with.

code.description: Closed set of tool-execution error codes.

rate_limit.description: RATE_LIMITED only: snapshot of the server's X-RateLimit-* headers at rejection — any of { limit, remaining, reset_secs } the server sent.

retry_after_secs.description: RATE_LIMITED only: seconds to WAIT before retrying (from the server's Retry-After header, or a conservative default when absent). Do not retry sooner.

retryable.description: false means an identical retry cannot succeed — recovery needs a different call (follow suggested_next_actions).

description.description: What this suggested action achieves. Actions are suggestions, not required next steps.

tool.description: Tool to call. Absent for actions the user (not the agent) must take.

AUTH_FAILED.description: Authentication or authorization failed (HTTP 401/403). `auth_reason` distinguishes `invalid_credentials` (401 on a Midnight cloud call — invalid or expired token; run `mnm auth github` to obtain or refresh one), `insufficient_tier` (403 — the token is valid but the request is not permitted for the account, typically an access-tier restriction), and `invalid_embedding_key` (BYOK embed/rerank — VoyageAI rejected your `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, a DIFFERENT credential; set a valid `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, NOT `mnm auth github`). An identical retry cannot succeed; follow `suggested_next_actions`.

CLOUD_ERROR.description: The cloud API returned a transient or permanent error (genuine 5xx / transport failures; 429 and 401/403 have their own codes). Call `status` to diagnose if it persists.

EMBEDDING_MODEL_MISMATCH.description: The embedding model used for the query does not match the corpus's active model (FR-038 / D12). The cloud-provided `remediation` string is the next step; there is no suggested tool call because the mismatch is corpus-side.

details.corpus_model: string ({name}@{revision} of the corpus's active embedder)

INSTALL_FAILED.description: The skill file could not be written to the target harness directory.

INVALID_INPUT.description: An argument failed validation. Fix the arguments and retry.

NOT_FOUND.description: The requested chunk, document, or source does not exist. Re-derive the id (e.g. from a fresh search) before trying again.

RATE_LIMITED.description: The cloud rate-limited this request (HTTP 429). `retry_after_secs` is how long to WAIT before retrying (from the server's Retry-After header, or a conservative default when absent) — an immediate retry will just be rejected again and delay success. `rate_limit` snapshots the X-RateLimit-* headers. Call the `status` tool to see your standing budget.

details.rate_limit: object ({ limit, remaining, reset_secs } — whichever X-RateLimit-* headers the server sent)

error_envelope.description: Tool failures are MCP tool results with `isError: true` — not JSON-RPC errors. `structuredContent` carries `{ error: { code, retryable, message, ...details }, suggested_next_actions: [..] }`; the text content block carries agent-facing recovery guidance plus a trimmed `{"error":{"code","retryable"}}` JSON fence (for `RATE_LIMITED` the fence additionally carries `retry_after_secs`, so an agent keying off the fence alone still sees how long to wait). `code` is a closed set (below). `retryable: false` means an identical retry cannot succeed — recovery requires a different call; follow `suggested_next_actions` or the guidance text. The machine-readable JSON Schema for this envelope is published as the top-level `errorSchema` key in this document (generated from `crates/mnm-mcp/src/render.rs` `ErrorKind` / `ToolFailure`, so its `code` enum, this prose, and the code never drift).

title: midnight-manual MCP tools

tools.description: Search the Midnight Network documentation and code corpus (docs, SDK references, Compact language material, code examples). Returns ranked excerpts with confidence scores and source attribution. Use it whenever you need facts about Midnight, Compact, or the Midnight SDK — even for things you think you already know, since model training data on Midnight is frequently stale; verify here first. Code-heavy queries (function names, API signatures, error strings from code) benefit from code_mode=exclusive; conceptual queries should keep the default. For multi-query strategies, facet filters, or rerank control, use advanced_search. If 3 searches haven't found it, change strategy — broaden the query, switch mode, or switch to advanced_search for facet filters — rather than rephrasing the same query. In results, symbol_path is a flat list of symbol names (their order is not a containment hierarchy); the get_chunks family and get_document_chunks return the richer structured {kind, name, path} segments (path = ancestor symbol names, present for nested symbols).

code_mode.description: Code-vector fusion (dual embeddings): on (default for hybrid/vector) fuses a voyage-code-3 ranked list alongside the general results; off = general retrieval only; exclusive = code vectors replace the general vector list (best for API-shaped / code-identifier queries). Incompatible with mode=fts.

mode.description: hybrid (default) fuses keyword + semantic; fts is keyword-only (lowest latency); vector is semantic-only.

query.description: What you want to find, as natural language or code terms.

tools.name: search

corpus_code_embedding_model.description: Present when the code-vector half ran (code_mode != off).

confidence.description: Promoted copy of scores.confidence (top-level for direct reads).

rank.description: 1-based position in the returned result list.

rerank_score.description: Voyage relevance score; present only when a local (BYOK) rerank ran.

attribution.description: Source attribution that drove the dominant trust multiplier.

relevance_source.description: Which relevance term fed the confidence blend.

matched_queries.description: Indices of the fused queries that matched (advanced_search only; basic search strips this).

symbol_path.description: Flat list of symbol names (kind dropped; order is not a containment hierarchy). Empty for prose chunks. The get_chunks family and get_document_chunks return the richer structured `{kind, name, path}` segment form.

description.description: What this suggested action achieves. Actions are suggestions, not required next steps.

tool.description: Tool to call. Absent for actions the user (not the agent) must take.

tools.description: Full-control search over the Midnight corpus: fuse multiple queries (HyDE, expansion, step-back), restrict by facet filters, switch retrieval mode, and toggle reranking. Use when basic search comes up short or when the midnight-advanced-search skill prescribes a pattern. Call facets first to discover valid filter values. Result-shaping knobs: sort_by picks the ordering (trust = most authoritative first, score = cheap recon; a local rerank overrides it), min_confidence drops weak matches at the source, response_format=concise trims the scores block (bodies stay), rerank_model=rerank-2.5-lite for cheaper reranking. If 3 searches haven't found it, change strategy — broaden the query, switch mode, or drop filters — rather than rephrasing the same query. In results, symbol_path is a flat list of symbol names (their order is not a containment hierarchy); the get_chunks family and get_document_chunks return the richer structured {kind, name, path} segments (path = ancestor symbol names, present for nested symbols).

code_mode.description: Code-vector fusion (dual embeddings): on (default for hybrid/vector) fuses a voyage-code-3 ranked list alongside the general results; off = general retrieval only; exclusive = code vectors replace the general vector list (best for API-shaped / code-identifier queries). Incompatible with mode=fts.

filters.description: Per-facet filters. AND across keys, OR within any_of, exclude none_of. See the `facets` tool for corpus-derived values.

min_confidence.description: Drop results below this blended-confidence floor [0,1] before limit is applied (default 0 = keep all). Raise it to suppress weak matches instead of over-fetching and post-filtering yourself; the count dropped is reported as search_metadata.filtered_by_confidence. The floor always gates on blended confidence, even when sort_by orders by trust/relevance/score — it is not the sort key.

mode.description: hybrid (default) fuses keyword + semantic; fts is keyword-only; vector is semantic-only.

queries.description: 1-10 query variants fused with RRF (HyDE, expansion, step-back). One query = one-element array. Rate-limit cost is one token per distinct query.

rerank.description: Apply VoyageAI reranking against the first query (server-side, or locally with your own VOYAGE_API_KEY). Disable for lowest latency.

rerank_instructions.description: Optional rerank instruction (max 400 chars). Guides relevance: emphasize aspects, filter document kinds, or disambiguate terms. Replaces the derived default instruction. Keep it terse — instruction tokens are multiplied by the candidate-pool size. See the midnight-advanced-search skill for guidance.

rerank_model.description: Which Voyage rerank model to use when rerank is on. rerank-2.5-lite is faster and materially cheaper per token — the recon / large-candidate-pool choice; keep rerank-2.5 (the default) for final-answer precision. Ignored when rerank=false. Honored on both the server and local-BYOK rerank paths.

response_format.description: Result verbosity. detailed (default): each result keeps its full nested scores breakdown (rrf/vector/trust factors). concise: drop ONLY that scores block — every result still carries its full content body, ids, source_path, headings/symbols, plus the promoted top-level confidence + attribution. Reach for it when you don't need the raw scoring internals; it is NOT a bodies-off mode.

sort_by.description: Result ordering when NOT locally reranking. confidence (default): blended trust×relevance, the balanced pick. trust: most authoritative sources first, for provenance-sensitive answers. relevance: normalized query match only, ignoring trust. score: raw RRF fusion order, cheapest recon. NOTE: a local (BYOK) rerank re-orders the pool afterwards, so sort_by has no effect there — disable rerank to honor it.

version_match.description: Version-filter semantics: permissive (default) biases ranking and drops only breaking mismatches among version-declaring content; strict hard-filters to satisfying content only.

security_level.description: Active client-side content-guard level (default moderate). Governs whether returned content is wrapped in <<UNTRUSTED-…>> blocks and, at strict, whether flagged items are removed. This is the *standing* configured level, always reported here; what the guard actually did to a given response appears in that response's own `security` object (present only when the guard acted). Ordered least→most aggressive: disabled < low < moderate < high < strict.
